Rough path

Words: 1k Articles: 20
Analysis OurBigBook.com
A rough path augments a path with compatible higher-order iterated-integral data. The extra data records effects, such as signed area, that are not continuously determined by the first-level path in the uniform topology. A rough differential equation uses this enhancement to recover a continuous solution map for irregular drivers.

A control is a continuous nonnegative function on ordered pairs of times, zero on the diagonal and superadditive as displayed. It measures the size of increments of a rough path, typically through ∣Xs,t(k)​∣≤ω(s,t)k/p. Continuous finite variation gives suitable controls, which let local estimates be stated without tying them to a particular time parametrization.

For 2<p<3, its local expansion includes Vi​(Ys​)Xs,ti​+DVj​(Ys​)Vi​(Ys​)Xs,tij​, with a remainder controlled at order greater than one. For a smooth driver it is the usual controlled ordinary differential equation; for enhanced Brownian motion it is the corresponding Stratonovich equation.

Universal limit theorem

Words: 62
Rough differential equation OurBigBook.com
For sufficiently regular vector fields, for example bounded fields with bounded derivatives through order three when 2<p<3, the solution map of a rough differential equation exists uniquely and is locally continuous in the rough path metric. Ordinary differential equations driven by smooth approximations therefore converge whenever their enhanced drivers converge. The theorem makes the enhancement, rather than just the original path, the correct input for a continuous solution map.

Harmonic analysis decomposes functions into elementary oscillations, generalizing Fourier series and the Fourier transform. On a locally compact Abelian group the elementary oscillations are continuous unitary characters, and Haar measure supplies translation-invariant integration.

A nonempty collection of real continuous subharmonic functions on a connected Riemann surface is a Perron family if it is closed under pairwise maxima and harmonic lifting of a continuous subharmonic function on every relatively compact coordinate disk. Its pointwise supremum is either everywhere infinite or a harmonic function on a Riemann surface. At a point where the supremum is finite, take increasing disk lifts approaching that value. The Harnack inequality for harmonic functions gives a finite harmonic limit on the disk. Lifting their maxima with any other member gives a larger harmonic limit with the same value at the chosen point, hence the same limit by the strong maximum principle for harmonic functions. The supremum is therefore harmonic on that disk; connectedness propagates finiteness to the whole surface.

Spectral-radius three-circle inequality (Mr​(f)≤Mr0​​(f)1−θMr1​​(f)θ)

Words: 148 Articles: 1
Spectral radius OurBigBook.com
For a holomorphic Banach algebra-valued function, put Mr​(f)=sup∣z∣=r​r(f(z)). Apply the Hadamard three-circle theorem to the holomorphic powers f2n. The continuous functions ∥f(z)2n∥1/2n decrease to the spectral radius. Supremum convergence for decreasing continuous functions passes the boundary suprema to the limit, proving the inequality with the same logarithmic interpolation parameter. In particular, at the geometric-mean radius, the square of the middle spectral radius is at most the product of the two boundary suprema.

Spectral-radius Liouville theorem

Words: 85
Spectral-radius three-circle inequality OurBigBook.com
If an entire Banach algebra-valued function has bounded spectral radius, that spectral radius is constant. The spectral-radius three-circle inequality on circles about an arbitrary point, with the outer radius tending to infinity, bounds every interior value by the maximum on any smaller circle. Upper semicontinuity of the spectral radius then lets the smaller radius tend to zero. Every value is bounded by the value at the arbitrary center; exchanging centers gives equality. The algebra-valued function itself can be nonconstant, for example zN for a fixed nonzero square-zero matrix N.

Joint spectral radius (ρ​(A)=limp→∞​maxAi​∈A​∥Ap​⋯A1​∥1/p)

Words: 80
Spectral radius OurBigBook.com
The joint spectral radius measures the worst exponential growth under arbitrary products from a finite family of matrices. Submultiplicativity gives its existence and invariance under changes of the chosen norm. Every fixed-length product B satisfies ρ(B)1/p≤ρ​(A), while the maximum norm of all length-p products to the power 1/p is an upper bound. A repeated product gives the first inequality; grouping an arbitrary long word into blocks proves the second. The spectral radius of each individual matrix does not control growth of all switched products.

Power-decay characterization of the spectral radius ((x/t)n→0⟺t>r(x),t>0)

Words: 61
Spectral radius formula OurBigBook.com
In a complex unital Banach algebra, the spectral radius formula makes the root norms of (x/t)n tend to r(x)/t. If t>r(x), those norms are eventually bounded above by a geometric sequence and the powers vanish. Conversely, vanishing powers eventually have norm less than one; the infimum version of the radius formula then forces r(x)/t<1. Consequently r(x)=inf{t>0:(x/t)n→0}, including the case r(x)=0.

Sturm oscillation theorem

Words: 69
Sturm-Liouville theory OurBigBook.com
For a real one-dimensional Sturm-Liouville problem with separated self-adjoint boundary conditions and discrete simple spectrum, the eigenfunction for the nth eigenvalue has exactly n interior zeros, numbering from zero. For a confining real Schrödinger operator on the line, the same ordering makes the ground state nodeless and the first excited state have one node. If the potential is even, uniqueness and reflection symmetry imply that these states are respectively even and odd.

Front solution

Words: 164 Articles: 2
Travelling wave OurBigBook.com
A front is a spatial profile connecting different asymptotic states on its two sides. A travelling wave front moves with a constant speed; a stationary front has zero speed. In a one-dimensional stationary reduction it is a heteroclinic orbit between the corresponding homogeneous equilibria. Equal first-integral values are necessary for a stationary front in a scalar conservative spatial equation.

Maxwell balance for a scalar reaction-diffusion front

Words: 52
Front solution OurBigBook.com
A stationary front solution of ut​=uxx​+f(u) connecting equilibria u−​ and u+​ requires ∫u−​u+​​f(s)ds=0. Multiply the stationary equation by ux​ and integrate: the derivative term has zero endpoint contribution. This equal-potential condition is the Maxwell balance. For f(u)=μu+αu3−u5, a front from zero to a nonzero constant requires u+2​=3α/4 and μ=−3α2/16.

Mesa solution

Words: 57
Front solution OurBigBook.com
A mesa is a localized broad plateau joined to its surrounding state by two separated fronts. Its leading spatial average equals the plateau fraction times the plateau value; the transition layers give corrections proportional to their width divided by the domain length. A conserved mean can determine the fraction occupied by the plateau, as in the coexistence fraction of a conserved-field amplitude mesa.

Fisher's equation (ut​=DΔu+ru(1−u/K))

Words: 31
Travelling wave OurBigBook.com
Fisher's equation is a reaction-diffusion equation combining diffusion with logistic growth. For positive D,r,K, one-dimensional fronts joining K to zero have minimum speed 2Dr​. The phase-plane construction of a Fisher travelling front and the linearized leading edge explain this threshold.

Phase-plane construction of a Fisher travelling front (c≥2k​)

Words: 82
Travelling wave OurBigBook.com
For ut​=uxx​+u(k−u) with k>0, a decreasing travelling wave connecting k to 0 satisfies w′=p, p′=−cp−w(k−w). If c≥2k​, choose a>0 with a(c−a)≥k. The triangle 0≤w≤k, −aw≤p≤0 is forward invariant: on its sloping side, (p+aw)′=w[a(c−a)−k+w]≥0. The descending unstable manifold of the saddle equilibrium (k,0) stays in this triangle and tends to (0,0), producing a positive heteroclinic orbit. Below the threshold the origin is a stable spiral for positive c, forcing sign changes; at c=0 conserved energy also excludes the connection.

Fixed-point theorem

Analysis OurBigBook.com
A fixed-point theorem gives conditions under which a map T has a point satisfying Tx=x.

Strict distance decrease on a compact metric space (d(fx,fy)<d(x,y)(x=y))

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Fixed-point theorem OurBigBook.com
A self-map f of a nonempty compact metric space satisfying the displayed strict distance inequality has exactly one fixed point, although a uniform contraction constant need not exist. The inequality makes f Lipschitz continuous with constant at most one, so g(x)=d(fx,x) is continuous and attains a minimum at p. If fp=p, then g(fp)<g(p), a contradiction. Two different fixed points contradict the same distance inequality.

Bounded-orbit fixed point for a strictly distance-decreasing Euclidean map

Words: 44
Strict distance decrease on a compact metric space OurBigBook.com
For a strictly distance-decreasing map of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, one bounded forward orbit suffices for existence of a fixed point. Its closure is compact by the Heine-Borel theorem and invariant by continuity, so strict distance decrease on a compact metric space applies. Strict distance decrease gives uniqueness throughout the whole space, not merely the orbit closure.

Kakutani fixed-point theorem

Words: 30
Fixed-point theorem OurBigBook.com
A nonempty compact convex set K in a finite-dimensional space and an upper hemicontinuous set-valued mapping F:K⇉K with nonempty closed convex values admit x∈F(x). A closed graph suffices when the whole output space is compact.

Words: 47
Fixed-point theorem OurBigBook.com
Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a locally convex space has a fixed point. Compactness is in the locally convex topology, which may be weaker than a norm topology. This version permits fixed-point arguments on a weak-star topology compact set of linear functionals. See Hartman's fixed-point chapter, Theorem 0.2.

Fixed-point theorem OurBigBook.com
Let T be a compact continuous self-map of a Banach space. If the set of solutions of u=tT(u) for 0≤t≤1 is bounded, then T has a fixed point. The theorem converts a priori estimates for a homotopy of equations into existence.

Fixed-point theorem OurBigBook.com
Every monotone self-map of a complete lattice has a complete lattice of fixed points. Its least fixed point is the meet of its prefixed points, and its greatest fixed point is the join of its postfixed points.

Contraction mapping theorem OurBigBook.com
For contraction mappings f,g, compare their fixed points using f on both arguments, then bound the change from f to g by the uniform metric. The resulting inequality gives the displayed estimate. Contraction property of closed subsets characterizes completeness

Words: 53
Contraction mapping theorem OurBigBook.com
A metric space is complete if and only if every contraction mapping of every nonempty closed subset into itself has a fixed point. For the converse, a nonconvergent Cauchy sequence contains a rapidly approaching subsequence whose point set is closed and whose shift is a contraction without a fixed point. Requiring the property only on the whole space is a different, weaker condition.

Contraction property under equivalent metrics
Words: 72
Contraction mapping OurBigBook.com
The same self-map can be a contraction mapping for one metric but not for a bilipschitz equivalent metric. On three points with distances d′(x,y)=d′(x,z)=2, d′(y,z)=1, the map f(x)=y, f(y)=f(z)=z has Lipschitz constant 1/2. For the discrete metric, its Lipschitz constant is one. The metrics satisfy d≤d′≤2d, so they preserve topology and completeness but not the strict numerical contraction condition. A contraction mapping theorem fixed-point proof therefore needs the specified metric and its contraction constant.

d(xλ​,xλ0​​)≤1−kd(Tλ​xλ0​​,Tλ0​​xλ0​​)​.

Iterated contraction

Words: 51
Contraction mapping theorem OurBigBook.com
If a self-map T of a nonempty complete metric space has an iterate Tn that is a contraction mapping, the contraction mapping theorem gives a unique fixed point a of Tn. The maps commute, so Tn(Ta)=T(Tna)=Ta, and uniqueness forces Ta=a. Conversely every fixed point of T is fixed by Tn. Thus a is the unique fixed point of T.

Root mean square (xrms​=⟨x2⟩​)

Words: 64
Analysis OurBigBook.com
The root mean square of a real function or data set is the square root of its mean square. A sinusoid of amplitude a has root mean square ∣a∣/2​. For orthogonal or uncorrelated zero-mean components, the squared root mean square of their sum is the sum of their mean squares; this follows by expanding the square and observing that all cross terms average to zero.

Full width at half maximum (FWHM)

Words: 42
Analysis OurBigBook.com
For a single-peaked profile, the full width at half maximum is the distance between the two positions where its value reaches half the peak above the specified background. It is often used to report the width of a point spread function or a spectral feature.
